The Trunk of the Elephant Curve Is You
The Greatest Boom in History Skipped You
description:
Extreme poverty collapsed from 38% of humanity to under 10% in a single generation. Your paycheck never got the memo.


KEY TAKEAWAYS:
• 38% of humanity lived in extreme poverty in 1990. Today it's under 10% — and the global Gini fell from ~0.70 to the low 0.60s, the first sustained drop since the Industrial Revolution.
• The inversion: as the gap BETWEEN countries shrank, the gap INSIDE them exploded. The US top 1% wealth share climbed from ~24% in 1989 to roughly 31% now.
• In 1975 the world income curve had two humps — a poor world and a rich world. By 2015 they had merged into one. The distribution that separated nations quietly stopped existing.
• From 1988 to 2008, the flattest real income gains on Earth went to the 80th–90th global percentile: the Western working and lower-middle class. That's the trunk of the elephant, and that's you.
